comments.body:
BLOCKED on frowsy-beggarly-mammoth's gate fix. Gerrit change 1615 (patch set 2) is complete and carries LLM-Review +1, but cannot obtain Verified +1 for a reason unrelated to this work.

Root cause, reproduced: .github/mutation-shards.toml lists .github/workflows/test.yml in global_support, and scripts/mutation_gate.py::select_shards returns tuple(manifest.shards) - every shard - when ANY changed path matches a global_support pattern, overriding the all-shards:false workflow input. This ticket must edit test.yml (AC6: the pytest -m external lane is one of the six unguarded lanes in scope), so the change selects all 7 shards (signing, reducer-processors, next-batch, gates, validate, compact-policy, push-policy) = 14 base+head mutation passes inside _mutation.yml's timeout-minutes: 30. Verified locally against this diff: 'SELECTED: all 7 => all shards selected? True'.

It is a timeout, not a flake or a race: two independent runs cancelled at the same mark - run 31560638673 at 30m16s (03:39:25->04:09:41) and run 31562494026 at 30m17s (04:16:23->04:46:40). GitHub reports a timed-out job as 'cancelled', which the CI bot converts to Verified -1. recheck therefore cannot clear it; I stopped rechecking after proving this.

Everything else is green on both runs: all four pytest cells passed (no s3_doctor flake on the second), and no --timeout fired anywhere, so the per-test budgets added by this ticket are not implicated in any failure.

Resolution path (operator decision): a dedicated agent is implementing frowsy-beggarly-mammoth as (1) drop .github/workflows/test.yml from global_support and (2) a measured raise of the mutation job's timeout-minutes in the SAME change - the second part is what lets the fix pass its own gate, since mutation-shards.toml is itself in global_support and would otherwise self-block. No admin bypass.

Next action on this ticket: once that fix merges to origin/main, rebase 1615 onto fresh origin/main (keeping the Change-Id), re-push, collect both votes, submit, then verify ACs and close. No code change is expected here - the work itself is done and reviewed.

compiled_state.description:
Discovered while fixing the ubuntu/py3.11 hang (89d5-61da-b621-47f8): _build-and-test.yml's
shared suite carries `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, but every OTHER CI pytest
invocation has NO per-test hang guard. `timeout-minutes` only bounds a whole job, so one
deadlocked test hides behind the last `-q` dot with no traceback and no culprit named — and
none of the affected lanes declares `timeout-minutes` at all, so they run under GitHub's
360-minute default.

Triage named six unguarded lanes; a sweep of .github/workflows found two more
(`_eval-discipline`, `_optionality`). All eight are fixed here so the class is closed.

## Operator decision applied

The operator decision (2026-08-10): per-lane budgets calibrated from historical runtime data,
generous allowance for live-service variance; do NOT copy one blanket timeout across lanes.
Applied as an auditable rule:

**Per-test budget = at least 10x the lane's observed mean per-test duration, floored at 300s.**

Durations came from recent successful Actions runs, reading each pytest step's
`started_at`/`completed_at` (runs 30986591446, 30964805133, 31003041092, 30983268038).
`--timeout-method=thread` is used everywhere for the same load-bearing reason as the shared
suite: the default `signal` method arms SIGALRM in the main thread and cannot fire while a
worker is blocked in a C-level flock/socket/subprocess call — exactly the hang shape these
lanes exercise.

| Lane | Observed evidence | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| ext-integ `external-llm` (live LLM matrix) | 16 tests, step 138-870s (bedrock 347->870s) | 900 |
| ext-integ `external` (live Jira Cloud) | 19 tests, step 85-120s | 600 |
| ext-integ `langfuse-trace` | 1 test, 24-29s | 300 |
| ext-integ `jira-dc-harness` | 63 tests, 2384-2635s (~41s/test mean) | 900 |
| structured-output-baseline | 1 test drives the whole sweep, 65-173s | 3600 |
| test.yml `external` | no run history (see below) | 600 |
| _eval-discipline | offline unit tests | 300 |
| _optionality degradation-path | offline unit tests | 300 |

Three budgets need a basis beyond the rule:

- **test.yml `external`** has NEVER executed (gated on a `workflow_dispatch` input never fired;
  its credential env keys are all commented out), so it has no history. It takes the same 600s
  as external-integration.yml's `external` lane, which runs the same `-m external` selection.
- **structured-output-baseline** is a SINGLE test driving the whole sweep, sized by the dispatch
  input `max_calls` (default 300 live calls). A budget sized to the observed 173s would truncate
  a deliberately larger human-dispatched sweep, so it gets 3600s — 20x the worst observation.
- **jira-dc-harness**'s 900s also clears by 3x the in-test field-readiness wait
  (`JIRA_DC_FIELD_READY_TIMEOUT`, default 120s, raisable to 300s per
  tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md), which runs INSIDE a test and is charged to the
  per-test budget.

## Dependency availability

Seven of eight lanes need no dependency work: `pytest-timeout==2.4.0` is pinned in the `dev`
extra (pyproject.toml) and each installs `--extra dev`. The exception is `_optionality.yml`'s
degradation-path step, which runs in a deliberately minimal `/tmp/clean` venv installing only
`pytest jsonschema mcp` so `agents_extra_installed()` stays False. `pytest-timeout` is added to
that install line rather than carving a permanent exemption into the new parity assertion: it
is a test-harness tool like the `pytest` already installed there, it is not part of the agents
stack whose ABSENCE the lane proves, and it installs in a LATER step than the clean-core-wheel
`find_spec` assertions — so what the lane proves is unchanged.

## Anti-regression

`tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py` asserts the guard only against `_build-and-test.yml`
via `_pytest_suite_run_blocks`, which filters on `"pytest -m" in run and "--dist" in run` —
blind twice over: `--dist` excludes every non-xdist lane, and `pytest -m` misses both
`python -m pytest` and a bare `pytest tests/...`. It is replaced by an exhaustive sweep over
EVERY .github/workflows file, with the detection rule specified here rather than left to
implementation choice.

**Detection rule.** Parse each workflow, walk `jobs.*.steps[]`, take each step's `run` body,
split into lines and DISCARD any line whose first non-whitespace character is `#` (a shell
comment; YAML comments never survive parsing). On each surviving line, match a pytest command
token at a command boundary:

    (?:^|\|\s*|&&\s*|;\s*)\s*(?:[\w./-]*/)?(?:python[\d.]*\s+-m\s+pytest|pytest)\b

Start-of-line or a `|`/`&&`/`;` separator, an optional path prefix, then `python -m pytest` or
`pytest` — independent of `-m` and of `--dist`. A matching step is a pytest lane and MUST carry
both `--timeout=` and `--timeout-method=thread` somewhere in that body (flags may sit on a
continuation line, so the assertion is against the whole body). Checked against the four forms
that occur and the near-misses it must NOT claim:

| Text | Detected? | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest -m "external and llm_live" ... -q` | yes | bare token at line start |
| `pytest tests/external/test_structured_output_matrix.py -q` | yes | line start, no `-m` |
| `python -m pytest -q \` | yes | `python -m pytest` form |
| `/tmp/clean/bin/python -m pytest \` | yes | path-prefixed `python` |
| `# --timeout (pytest-timeout) is the ... GUARD` | no | comment line, discarded |
| `/tmp/clean/bin/pip install pytest pytest-timeout` | no | argument to pip, not at a command boundary |

The last row is load-bearing: `_optionality.yml` installs pytest by name on a `pip install`
line, so a bare-substring matcher would demand a timeout flag on an install step.

Alongside the universal assertion the sweep carries a liveness one: the discovered lane set
must COVER a known-expected set spanning all four forms, so a refactor that breaks the matcher
fails loudly instead of passing vacuously over zero lanes. New lanes need no test edit — they
simply must be guarded.

## Acceptance Criteria

In external-integration.yml, each step gains `--timeout-method=thread` plus:

- [ ] AC1: `pytest -m "external and llm_live"` carries `--timeout=900`.
- [ ] AC2: `pytest -m "external and not llm_live"` carries `--timeout=600`.
- [ ] AC3: the Langfuse trace step carries `--timeout=300`.
- [ ] AC4: the Jira DC harness step carries `--timeout=900`.
- [ ] AC5: structured-output-baseline.yml's pytest step carries `--timeout=3600
      --timeout-method=thread`.
- [ ] AC6: test.yml's `pytest -m external` step carries `--timeout=600
      --timeout-method=thread`.
- [ ] AC7: _eval-discipline.yml and _optionality.yml's pytest steps each carry
      `--timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread`, and _optionality.yml's clean venv installs
      `pytest-timeout` so the flag is honored instead of erroring as an unknown option.
- [ ] AC8: tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py implements the detection rule above and fails
      if ANY pytest-invoking step in ANY .github/workflows file lacks either flag. Proven by
      removing a flag from a lane of EACH of the four forms in turn (`pytest -m` in
      external-integration.yml, bare `pytest <path>` in structured-output-baseline.yml,
      `python -m pytest` in _eval-discipline.yml, path-prefixed in _optionality.yml) and seeing
      a failure each time; passes on the committed tree.
- [ ] AC8b: the sweep does NOT flag non-invoking text — _optionality.yml's `pip install pytest
      pytest-timeout` line and _build-and-test.yml's `# --timeout (pytest-timeout)` comment are
      not lanes — and its discovered set covers all four forms, so a broken matcher cannot pass
      vacuously.
- [ ] AC9: each per-lane budget and its evidence is recorded as a YAML comment at the step it
      governs, so the number is auditable at the point of use.
- [ ] AC10: workflows stay valid — `make lint` (runs actionlint) and `make typecheck` pass, and
      no lane's selection, markers, or behavior changes beyond the added flags.

file_impact.reason: Add per-test --timeout/--timeout-method=thread hang guards to the four unguarded pytest steps (llm_live matrix 900s, live Jira Cloud 600s, Langfuse trace 300s, Jira DC harness 900s), each with its calibration rationale as a YAML comment.
Add --timeout=3600 --timeout-method=thread to the structured-output matrix pytest step; 3600s because the lane is a single test driving a dispatch-sized sweep (max_calls default 300).
Add --timeout=600 --timeout-method=thread to the pytest -m external step; calibrated by analogy to the external-integration external lane since this job has never executed.
Add --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread to the offline eval-discipline pytest step (unguarded lane found by the full workflow sweep).
Add --timeout=300 --timeout-method=thread to the degradation-path pytest step and add pytest-timeout to the clean minimal venv so the flag is honored.
Extend the hang-guard assertion from _build-and-test.yml only to an exhaustive sweep of every pytest-invoking step in every .github/workflows file, so a new lane cannot ship unguarded.
